title: Post-rollforward Incident Drill and Release Schedule Notes (Aug 2026) - Draft
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft for a scheduled post-rollforward incident drill and aligned release-week schedule notes. The goal is to validate our detection + mitigation + communication paths after a rollforward (a controlled advance of a release across regions). We also collect a short draft of release notes items that should be published once the canary completes.

Scope and context:
- Applies to major and minor rollforwards that include runtime or routing changes (examples: inference-runtime v1.9.x, routing-proxy config updates, batch scheduler adjustments).
- Not for pure docs-only or dashboard-only changes.
- This drill assumes Dedicated and Hosted clusters are both in the rollout path; private deployments will be included where customers opt-in.

High-level objectives (what we validate):
1) Canary/mini-canary telemetry triggers within defined SLO thresholds (latency, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization).
2) Automated fallback (route to previous model variant or region) executes within target time when thresholds breached.
3) Oncall and release team communications are clear, with a post-drill incident stub created and evidence collected for a postmortem.
4) Release notes capture actual behavior changes, known limitations, and migration steps.

Planned drill date(s) and calendar (working schedule, will lock 72h prior):
- 2026-08-25 10:00-11:30 PDT: Internal drill run (global canary on non-production stage)
- 2026-09-01 09:00-12:00 PDT: Week-of-release rehearsal (full canary into blue pool, includes oncall rotation)
- Safety windows: 09:00-12:00 local time for primary regions. No customer-visible migrations outside windows unless approved by Eng Leads.
- Contingency window: 12:00-14:00 same day reserved for rollback and dryness checks.

Pre-drill checklist (owners in parenthesis):
- Preconditions
  - Confirm preflight CI green for rollout branch (Infra CI lead)
  - Verify canary config: percentage, target regions, metrics endpoints, webhook for alerting (Release engineer)
  - Ensure latest smoke-test suite committed to infra repo and referenced by release job (QA)
  - Create ephemeral release Slack channel: #release-2026-08-rollforward (Communications)
  - Notify stakeholders: SRE, Observability, Product, Support (Release PM)

- Observability checks to verify before starting (SRE lead):
  - Baseline latency p50/p90/p99 for redwood-api and inference-runtime using last 7 days
  - Baseline GPU utilization for Dedicated pools under expected load
  - Confirm tracing spans for key RPCs propagate (client->proxy->runtime)
  - Alert hooks: PagerDuty escalation path, Slack webhook, incident creation template present

Drill run steps (live playbook):
1) Start canary to 3% traffic in us-west1 (Release engineer triggers job).
2) Run smoke test suite against canary endpoints (QA / automated). Fail criteria: any smoke-test failing or p90 latency > baseline + 30%.
3) Monitor metrics for first 10 minutes:
   - p50/p90/p99 latency for generation endpoints (redwood-api/generate)
   - 5m error rate rolling window > 0.5% triggers warning, > 2% triggers critical
   - GPU memory OOM signs, backpressure logs from scheduler
4) If warning threshold hit: pause increase, expand telemetry logging (SRE).
5) If critical threshold hit: execute automated fallback to previous variant and open incident (Release engineer + SRE).
6) Post-fallback verification: ensure canary traffic had fallback applied and user requests served with previous variant within 120s.

Incident stub template to create (on fallback/critical):
- Title: Post-rollforward incident stub — <short description>
- Severity: sev2 by default for production user impact, sev3 for degraded non-blocking issues
- Teams paged: eng-release, eng-sre, infra-observability, product
- First 30-min actions: collect logs (first and last 5 mins), trace links, canary job config, commit sha, exact timestamps

Rollback / Rollforward decision matrix (simplified):
- If error-rate > 2% OR p99 latency > baseline * 2 for > 5 minutes -> immediate rollback to previous image/variant (automated path if configured)
- If GPU OOMs observed OR model quality regressions confirmed by eval set -> rollback and block further promotion
- If increase is < 15% in p90 without user-visible failures -> consider throttle & extended observation, no rollback

Communication play (who messages what):
- On start: #release-2026-08-rollforward pinned message with canary link, job id, owners (Release PM)
- On warning: SRE posts metrics snapshot, tagging oncall and release engineer
- On critical + fallback: Release lead posts public internal update (Slack + Status page draft), triage channel invites Data Science for quality assessment
- After drill: short summary posted in release channel within 60 minutes, full notes in Confluence within 48h

Artifacts to capture during drill (automated where possible):
- Canary job id and logs (infra job artifacts)
- Grafana dashboard snapshots for the 10-minute window around trigger
- Kafka topic offset snapshots for request queues
- A small sample of failing requests and corresponding traces (strip PII)

Smoke tests (short list that must run):
- healthcheck on redwood-api (GET /health)
- short generation (max tokens 64) across two model families
- streaming response test (websocket/stream endpoint)
- KV-cache warmup roundtrip for cached prefix paths

Rollout cadence notes (how to pace after canary completes successfully):
- 0-1 hour: increase to 10% in same region if stable for 15m
- 1-3 hours: 25% then 50% after 30m stable windows
- 3-6 hours: expand to other low-latency regions (eu-west1) at 10% then ramp as above
- Full global promotion only after 6h stable and signoff from SRE and Release PM

Draft release notes (to be refined before public posting):
- Summary: "Rolling update to inference-runtime v1.9.2 and routing-proxy v0.45. Changes improve concurrent batch scheduling and reduce cold-start latency for medium-length prompts."
- Key changes:
  - Scheduler: new burst handling reduces queue wait under high concurrent batch loads (expected 10-20% p90 improvement in synthetic load tests)
  - Runtime: kernel selection heuristic updated for decoder-only models (should improve throughput for Llama-family models)
  - Routing: fallback policy can now route to pinned variant on capacity pressure (config opt-in)
- Known issues:
  - Small subset of legacy quantized models may show increased memory pressure on older GPUs; automatic fallback triggers should prevent user impact
  - Some internal telemetry tags changed; dashboards updated but old widgets may lag until next sync
- Action for integrators: no code changes required. If you pin model variants, expect the fallback behavior if capacity is constrained.

Post-drill deliverables and timeline:
- Immediate: incident stub + short summary in Slack (within 60m)
- Day 0-2: collect artifacts and complete a 1-page "Drill Evidence" doc (SRE)
- Day 3: consolidate a short postmortem with clear action items and owners (Release lead)
- Day 7: verify all action items closed or on a tracked plan; if high-severity findings, schedule follow-up remediation sprint

Open questions (to resolve before final run):
- Should we include private deployment customers in automated fallback tests? (security/ops signoff needed)
- Is the automated rollback path allowed to run without manual confirmation in Dedicated clusters? (legal/enterprise policy)
- Are we comfortable with 3% initial canary on high-throughput endpoints, or should we start at 1%?

Appendix: Quick run commands and links (ops cheatsheet)
- Canary job triggers: infra CI -> Deploy job id format: deploy-rollforward-<sha>-<timestamp>
- Grafana: dashboards/RE/rollforward-canary (bookmark this prior to run)
- PagerDuty escalation: Team = eng-release -> Level 1: oncall@redwood.ai -> Level 2: release-lead@redwood.ai
- Artifact storage: s3://redwood-release-artifacts/2026-08-rollforward/<job-id>/

Notes for reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; the playbook steps will be extracted to the main Rollforward Playbook once validated by two drill runs.
- Feedback requested on thresholds (p90 % delta and error-rate thresholds) and communication cadence for external customers.

Draft edit log:
- 2026-08-10: created by Daniel Kim (initial outline)
- 2026-08-12: added fallback matrix and smoke test list (Priya Sharma)
- 2026-08-16: updated cadence ramp timings after SRE review (Miguel Torres)
- 2026-08-18: tightened alert thresholds and added incident stub template (Aisha Patel)

---
End of draft.
